body.hook: Many high school wind players have a comfortable range of about an octave and a half. Professional players often have two and a half or more. Range doesn't come from pressing harder; it comes from flexible muscles, fast air and patient daily practice.

vocabulary.definition: The span of notes from lowest to highest a player can play well.

study.title: Reaching Higher (and Lower)
study.question: How do I extend my range safely?
study.passage:
Principles:
• High notes need faster air and a firm, not pinched, embouchure.
• Low notes need relaxed, open, warm air.
• Never force high notes by pressing the mouthpiece harder into the lips (brass) or biting (woodwinds).
• Rest as much as you play.
Part 1, Warm-up (5 minutes): Long tones in the middle register.
Part 2, Flexibility (15 minutes):
• Brass: lip slurs on one valve combination, such as concert B♭ to F and back, then up to the next partial. Keep the air steady and let the lips do small adjustments.
• Woodwinds: register slurs (low to high with the register or octave key), and long tones at the top and bottom of the comfortable range.
• Flute: harmonic exercises (overblowing a low fingering to sound higher partials).
• Percussion: expand dynamic "range" with very soft to very loud strokes, and four-mallet or timpani tuning if available.
Part 3, Extend by one note (10 minutes): Play a scale up to your highest comfortable note, rest, then try one note higher with a big, fast breath. If it doesn't sound good, go back. Do the same downward.
Part 4, Range log: Record your lowest and highest good-sounding notes each week.

examples.title: Air speed
examples.problem: What kind of air helps high notes?
examples.answer: Faster, steady air with a firm embouchure

examples.title: Pressure
examples.problem: Why not press the mouthpiece harder for high notes?
examples.answer: It cuts off lip vibration, causes fatigue and can injure the lips

examples.title: Lip slurs
examples.problem: What changes in a lip slur?
examples.answer: Air and small lip adjustments, not fingerings

examples.title: Extending safely
examples.problem: You try one note higher and it squeaks. What next?
examples.answer: Return to your comfortable top note, rest, and try again another day
